A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hierarchical Refinement (HiRef) work. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, mouse-embryo alignments, MERFISH expression-transfer results, ImageNet alignment costs, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments with MOP, mini-batch OT, and MERFISH baseline runs without subsampling.

M1.justification: The recursive low-rank co-clustering procedure, uniform inner marginals, rank-schedule optimization, and distance-matrix approximation are retained. Select becomes Assign, and v2 corrects a source/target input symbol in the explanatory equation; both versions' algorithms already use the source and target datasets correctly.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic dataset pairs, seven consecutive MOSTA embryonic-stage alignments, two MERFISH slices with five expression-transfer genes, and ImageNet embedding alignment. The additional MERFISH subsampling variants change sample sizes within existing coverage.

E2.justification: V1 explicitly excludes MOP, whereas v2 evaluates it on the 512-point synthetic instances and MERFISH. V2 also adds mini-batch OT to MOSTA, MERFISH, and ImageNet comparisons. These introduce two important scalable comparator families beyond the retained Sinkhorn, ProgOT, FRLC, and LOT comparisons.

E3.justification: The evaluation gains systematic mini-batch configurations, including sampling without replacement and Sinkhorn regularization of 0.05, plus MOP runs using default GMRA partitions. MERFISH adds spatial transport cost and comparisons with and without source subsampling. Its reported FRLC budget changes from 200 to 20 outer iterations. Together these substantially extend the comparison design; the PDFs do not establish whether every revised existing result was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a targeted check of whether subsampling disadvantages FRLC and LOT. The new mini-batch results also examine batch-size sensitivity across the real-data tasks. The existing low-rank sensitivity analysis in Figure S3 is retained, with its discussion moved into Appendix D.1.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose synthetic-data generation seed 0 and MERFISH seed 44. Neither introduces repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests; the added result rows retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables S4 and S6–S8 add substantial MOP, mini-batch, and unsubsampled-baseline results. ImageNet mini-batch costs range from 21.89 to 19.58, while existing HiRef and FRLC costs are retained up to rounding. MOSTA HiRef cost for E12.5–E13.5 changes from 14.5741 to 14.35. MERFISH FRLC scores and FRLC/LOT runtimes are revised; LOT's original subsampled scores remain, while its higher main-text scores now come from the new unsubsampled condition. These are not all comparable-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The proof of Proposition B.2 restores a factor of 2 in the added/subtracted sum and aligns its closing distinctness condition with the proposition's requirement on all cost entries. The central propositions and bounds remain. V2's named hierarchical block-coupling definition restates a formula already present in v1 and Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the low-rank co-clustering invariant, hierarchical construction of bijective full-rank couplings, linear-space/log-linear-time scaling, and feasibility on million-point datasets. The additional comparisons support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of batch-size-dependent mini-batch error and MERFISH subsampling effects. Appendix D.3 explains the LOT cost-function/rank differences and cautions against comparing transport costs across different sample sizes. Section 5 expands the proposed use of precomputed global pairs for flow matching and registration; these remain suggested applications rather than evaluated tasks.

D1.justification: V2 discloses default Sinkhorn regularization, MOP partition construction, and mini-batch sampling details. Appendix D.4 specifies 167 discarded ImageNet images, 640500 samples per split, the Euclidean cost, and corresponding distance-factor ranks. Appendix D.3 newly explains LOT's squared-Euclidean fallback, but removes v1's explicit FRLC distance-factorization rank statement. Code availability is unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially expand positioning around mini-batch estimators, partial/unbalanced transport, and two-scale hierarchical OT. Added works include Fatras et al. (2020, 2021b), Nguyen et al. (2022a, 2022b), Schmitzer and Schnorr (2013), and Gaussian-mixture transport papers. V2 distinguishes these approaches from its progressive refinement and removes the De Bortoli et al. (2021) discussion. Publication updates to retained references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: V2 refines the abstract and explanatory prose, expands the rank-annealing explanation, standardizes much of 'transport plan' to 'coupling,' and renames Section 3. Some discussion moves between the main text and appendix, and an Impact Statement is added. The overall six-section narrative and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 switches from a linear to a logarithmic sample-size axis and improves label readability. Main-text benchmark tables are consolidated and relocated, with early embryonic results retained in Table S6. Tables S4 and S6–S8 expand their rows or columns, especially S7's transport-cost column. Algorithm 3 moves, and Figures S2–S3 shrink to accommodate it; the principal mapping illustrations remain.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evaluation by testing scalable alternatives omitted from v1 and checking the MERFISH subsampling confound. Added implementation details and Figure 2's logarithmic axis also aid assessment. The gain is limited by reporting problems: Table S7 combines transport costs using different cost functions, and Section 4.1 describes MOP's checkerboard cost as twice as high although Table S4 shows approximately three times HiRef's cost. The expanded evidence is useful, but these issues constrain its interpretation.
